documents.title: Start with the CSS you already have.
documents.summary: Audit first, compile when it adds value, and keep the browser contract ordinary.

sections.title: Install the release candidate
sections.body: The 0.1.0-rc.3 compatibility unit is under exact-source verification. Use this command after all nineteen crates are published and replayed with Rust 1.85.

sections.title: Audit ordinary CSS
sections.body: Start without changing authoring. The analyzer emits human, canonical JSON, or SARIF findings and fails closed on unknown surfaces.

sections.title: Add typed identities selectively
sections.body: Rust literals are validated at compile time and compile to static standards-compliant CSS. There is no styling runtime.

documents.title: Types at author time. CSS at run time.
documents.summary: Stable 128-bit identities connect Rust source, emitted classes, manifests, and physical declarations.

sections.title: One literal, one stable identity
sections.body: pc! accepts one visible string literal. The macro parses semantics, rejects conflicting slots, and returns a sealed Style.

sections.title: Visible state spaces
sections.body: pcx! compiles every visible branch combination and selects one identity at runtime. Independent clauses that can collide are rejected.

sections.title: Follow the physical effect
sections.body: Manifest schema 5 joins semantic declarations to final rules, conditions, byte ranges, and synthesized effects such as box-shadow.

documents.title: Standards-first, not framework-first.
documents.summary: Analyze standard CSS, enforce policy, and transform output without claiming ownership of authored source.

sections.title: Bounded classification
sections.body: The classifier recognizes deliberate standard-CSS surfaces and reports unsupported constructs instead of guessing. A versioned corpus controls the claim.

sections.title: Deterministic transformation
sections.body: Target browsers, minify, and check output drift. Add --check in CI to remain read-only.
sections.code:
pliego-cssc transform-css --input app.css \
  --output dist/app.css --targets modern --format minified

sections.title: Compatibility, accessibility, and budgets
sections.body: Policy documents bind findings to explicit targets and limits. The same canonical findings feed terminals, JSON automation, and SARIF.

documents.title: A green build should explain itself.
documents.summary: Artifacts carry hashes, source lineage, graphs, findings, and receipts designed for replay.

sections.title: Canonical manifests
sections.body: Style identity, class identity, theme identity, origins, conditions, physical declarations, and final CSS hashes live in a deterministic document.

sections.title: Receipt-last publication
sections.body: Controlled operations stage output, lock the destination, verify inputs, publish artifacts, and write the receipt last.

sections.title: Measured, inherited, pending, uncertain
sections.body: Release readiness preserves the evidence class. Old hosted evidence never silently passes changed source.

documents.title: Adopt without surrendering the exit.
documents.summary: Inventory first, generate bounded plans, preserve originals, and detect drift immediately before publication.

sections.title: Read-only discovery
sections.body: Tailwind, Sass, CSS Modules, and standard CSS can be inventoried before any replacement plan exists.

sections.title: Reversible replacements
sections.body: Plans bind source and destination hashes. Apply and rollback use adjacent locks, pre-publication revalidation, backups, and group compensation.

sections.title: No speculative codemods
sections.body: Unsupported or context-dependent constructs stay in the inventory. The migration layer does not infer framework semantics it cannot prove.

documents.title: Native together. Independent by contract.
documents.summary: PliegoRS is the first native consumer, not the only target. It supplies topology; PliegoCSS supplies style identity and artifacts.

sections.title: Explicit ownership
sections.body: PliegoRS owns routes, pages, assets, and browser lifecycle. PliegoCSS owns parsing, semantic conflicts, CSS, manifests, and policy findings.

sections.title: Route and island bundles
sections.body: A reachability sidecar projects application-owned topology into selected CSS bundles without PliegoCSS pretending to understand the framework.

sections.title: Replayed from published crates
sections.body: The maintained fixture locks PliegoRS 0.0.2 registry packages and verifies the remote-reachable framework revision separately.

documents.title: Choose an adoption surface.
documents.summary: Install the CLI for any project, add the Rust crates only when typed authoring belongs in the application.

sections.title: CLI-only adoption
sections.body: The command-line compiler can audit, transform, explain, bundle, and migrate standard CSS without adding a runtime dependency to the application.

sections.title: Typed Rust authoring
sections.body: Add pliego-css and its macro crate to applications that want compile-time style identities. The emitted result remains ordinary CSS.

sections.title: Pin the exact release identity
sections.body: Before the public release, use the signed project tag plus Cargo.lock. Do not track a moving branch in a production build.

documents.title: Learn before changing.
documents.summary: Run a read-only CSS audit, inspect canonical findings, then decide whether transformation or policy is justified.

sections.title: Read the first report
sections.body: Human output is optimized for local diagnosis. Every finding carries a stable code and source location rather than an opaque score.

sections.title: Feed automation safely
sections.body: Canonical JSON and SARIF preserve the same finding model for CI, code scanning, and archival evidence.
sections.code: pliego-cssc audit --input app.css --targets modern --format sarif > findings.sarif

sections.title: Unknown means unknown
sections.body: The standard-CSS classifier is bounded. Unsupported selectors, properties, or values fail closed under compatibility policy rather than being treated as safe.

documents.title: Put the compiler engine in the feedback loop.
documents.summary: Use `pliego-css-lsp` for diagnostics, completion, hover evidence, and catalog-aware authoring without launching the build CLI.

sections.title: VS Code extension
sections.body: The maintained extension launches `pliego-css-lsp`, discovers the project theme, and renders diagnostics in Rust source.

sections.title: Any LSP client
sections.body: Launch the server over stdio from the same workspace used by CI. The protocol stays editor-neutral.

sections.title: Bound in-process work
sections.body: Document versions debounce for 150 ms, stale results are suppressed, semantic caches are bounded, and each document stops at 256 checks with `PCL002`.

documents.title: A finite language with visible edges.
documents.summary: Utilities lower into semantic slots, conditions, and typed values before any CSS serialization occurs.

sections.title: Utility plus typed value
sections.body: Spacing, color, typography, layout, effects, and interactivity draw from one validated theme registry. Arbitrary escape hatches remain policy-visible.
sections.code: flex items-center gap-4 rounded-lg bg-surface px-4 py-2 text-sm

sections.title: Conditions are structure
sections.body: Responsive, state, attribute, container, layer, and media variants become normalized condition paths. Their order is not incidental string decoration.

sections.title: Importance follows the physical effect
sections.body: A trailing exclamation mark marks the semantic contribution important. Synthesized effects such as the composed box-shadow preserve that authority in final CSS and lineage.

documents.title: Compose by meaning, not source order.
documents.summary: Compatible slots commute. Conflicting slots require an explicit branch-over-base operation.

sections.title: Equivalent input, equivalent identity
sections.body: Utilities that occupy independent semantic slots canonicalize to the same identity even when authored in a different order.
sections.code:
flex gap-4 p-6
p-6 flex gap-4

sections.title: Ambiguous lists are rejected
sections.body: p-4 p-6 does not mean last one wins. Both declarations claim the same slot under the same condition, so compilation stops.

sections.title: Overrides are explicit operations
sections.body: When an application intentionally replaces one semantic assignment with another, use composition so the override relationship remains visible and inspectable.

documents.title: Conditions without string-order folklore.
documents.summary: Every variant joins a typed condition path with deterministic normalization and specificity behavior.

sections.title: Responsive paths
sections.body: Theme breakpoints are validated once and emitted as ordered media conditions. Assignments at different breakpoints do not conflict.

sections.title: State and attributes
sections.body: Pseudo-class and bounded attribute variants stay in semantic IR so policy and physical lineage can explain their selectors.

sections.title: Cascade layers
sections.body: Fixed layer variants model author-controlled precedence without allowing arbitrary source-order dependence to leak into identity.

documents.title: Resolve tokens before styles.
documents.summary: TOML themes and DTCG Resolver documents feed the same typed registry, identity, graph, and emitted variables.

sections.title: Extend the seed
sections.body: A project theme can override or add typed colors, spacing, radii, typography, and breakpoints without changing utility grammar.

sections.title: Select DTCG contexts explicitly
sections.body: Resolver inputs are never auto-discovered. Modifier selections participate in configuration identity even when two contexts resolve to equal values.

sections.title: Publish the complete Token Graph
sections.body: Controlled output binds selected CSS to canonical token provenance, aliases, permutations, and reachability-aware usage evidence.

documents.title: Make browser support and budgets executable.
documents.summary: Compatibility, accessibility, payload, package, route, and ownership policies turn expectations into reviewable inputs.

sections.title: Version the target
sections.body: baseline-widely and modern are frozen policy profiles with explicit browser and source-data identities. They do not drift silently with a dependency update.

sections.title: Bind budgets to owners
sections.body: Direct files can name budget subjects manually. Asset Plans use an ownership sidecar to aggregate package and composed-route costs without guessing responsibility.

sections.title: Audit static accessibility contracts
sections.body: Contrast and interaction guards use explicit policy plus token evidence. Dynamic visual behavior still requires browser and assistive-technology testing.

documents.title: Explain the winning declaration.
documents.summary: Inspect authored CSS by element and longhand to see matching selectors, precedence, and the final winner.

sections.title: Ask one precise question
sections.body: Provide a CSS file, a bounded element description, and one longhand. The command reports candidates instead of simulating an entire browser.

sections.title: See why it won
sections.body: Origin, importance, layer, specificity, and source position are surfaced in comparison order with a stable machine-readable form.

sections.title: Keep the model honest
sections.body: This is a static bounded inspector. Runtime DOM state, animation interpolation, adopted sheets, and script mutation remain browser responsibilities.

documents.title: Trace source intent into emitted bytes.
documents.summary: Manifest schema 5 connects source origins, semantic assignments, final selectors, physical declarations, and CSS ranges.

sections.title: Identity chain
sections.body: StyleId identifies canonical semantics. Class identity, theme identity, configuration, and final CSS hash bind that style into one build.

sections.title: Physical lineage
sections.body: Generated custom properties and synthesized declarations retain contributors, importance, conditions, selector, property, value, and output byte range.

sections.title: Request the schema you consume
sections.body: Schema 3 supports style manifests, schema 4 adds reachability ownership, and schema 5 adds closed physical tracing. Consumers must pin their contract.

documents.title: Publish the receipt last.
documents.summary: Controlled builds stage related outputs, lock the destination, verify hashes, compensate failures, and expose one completed receipt.

sections.title: One rollback-capable group
sections.body: CSS, source map, style manifest, Token Graph, findings, control manifest, and receipt are generated from one exact input snapshot.
sections.code:
pliego-cssc compile --source src --output dist/app.css \
  --manifest dist/app.manifest.json --control-dir dist

sections.title: Check without writing
sections.body: The same command with --check recomputes every artifact and fails on byte drift without taking publication locks or replacing files.
sections.code:
pliego-cssc compile --source src --output dist/app.css \
  --manifest dist/app.manifest.json --control-dir dist --check

sections.title: Completion is explicit
sections.body: Consumers treat the fixed receipt as the publication boundary. Its absence means the group is incomplete, even if individual files are present.

documents.title: Prove what rendered above the fold.
documents.summary: Join observed browser behavior to project topology and retained style identity without letting an observation silently authorize removal.

sections.title: Observe a real route
sections.body: Capture viewport, route, interaction state, loaded assets, matched styles, and source identities from a browser run against the built application.

sections.title: Join exact universes
sections.body: Evidence is accepted only when its project index, asset plan, reachability, and CSS identities match the build under review.

sections.title: Observation does not equal deletion
sections.body: A style unseen in one scope remains unknown outside that scope. Explicit retention and reachability policies control removal authority.

documents.title: Inventory Tailwind before translating it.
documents.summary: Recover the real utility surface, classify supported roles, and keep unsupported framework behavior visible.

sections.title: Scan without replacement
sections.body: The inventory recognizes bounded class-bearing surfaces and reports candidates with source ranges. It does not rewrite template semantics during discovery.

sections.title: Generate a hash-bound project plan
sections.body: A declaration selects roots and destinations. The plan records exact source and output hashes before any replacement can be applied.

sections.title: Preserve unsupported behavior
sections.body: Plugins, generated variants, arbitrary selectors, and runtime class construction remain explicit migration findings unless a project-owned adapter proves them.

documents.title: Separate syntax conversion from semantic adoption.
documents.summary: Inventory variables, nesting, mixins, imports, and generated surfaces without pretending every Sass abstraction is a utility.

sections.title: Map the source surface
sections.body: The inventory records statically visible Sass roles and unresolved dynamic behavior so the team can choose what stays authored CSS.

sections.title: Ordinary CSS is a valid destination
sections.body: Use the standard-CSS transformer for syntax and compatibility work. Adopt typed PliegoCSS styles only where identity and provenance pay for themselves.

sections.title: Keep originals and rollback evidence
sections.body: Applied replacements preserve source backups and hash-bound rollback records. A changed destination aborts rather than overwriting concurrent edits.

documents.title: Preserve component ownership.
documents.summary: Discover module exports and usage while keeping application-owned component topology separate from CSS semantics.

sections.title: Inventory exported classes
sections.body: The scanner identifies bounded module class definitions and their source locations without assuming a particular bundler naming strategy.

sections.title: Let the application own reachability
sections.body: Route and component reachability comes from the framework or product index, not from filename heuristics inside the CSS compiler.

sections.title: Mixed adoption is first-class
sections.body: A project can retain modules for component styles, audit their emitted CSS, and introduce typed identities only for new or shared surfaces.

documents.title: One CLI, explicit modes.
documents.summary: Compile, inspect, audit, transform, explain, bundle, watch, migrate, format, plan, and verify with strict argument contracts.

sections.title: Discover the real command surface
sections.body: Root and command help are generated from the maintained command synopsis. Unknown options, duplicate single-value options, and missing values fail.

sections.title: Select diagnostic transport globally
sections.body: Human and JSON diagnostics can be requested before or after the command without stealing option values that happen to resemble flags.

sections.title: Use --check in CI
sections.body: Commands that publish controlled or generated artifacts expose a read-only comparison path. CI should verify the checked-in or staged output, not regenerate it silently.

documents.title: Compiler feedback without editor subprocesses.
documents.summary: The LSP uses the same in-process `AnalysisHost` as CLI and watch without launching `pliego-cssc` or writing synthetic source files.

sections.title: Diagnostics, completion, and hover
sections.body: Visible `pc!` and `pcx!` literals receive shared diagnostics, catalog-backed completion, and compiler-emitted hover CSS under the exact active theme.

sections.title: Suppress stale document work
sections.body: Document versions are debounced for 150 ms, and version checks around bounded in-process analysis prevent obsolete results from being published.

sections.title: Bound analysis
sections.body: Each document is capped at 256 semantic checks, the shared cache is bounded and theme-invalidated, and excessive input emits `PCL002`.

documents.title: Keep the last complete truth.
documents.summary: Poll coherent snapshots, republish only valid groups, and retain the last valid output across transient edits.

sections.title: Watch inputs and output
sections.body: The watcher accepts the same source, theme, target, format, manifest, reachability, and controlled-output options as compile.

sections.title: Confirm one coherent snapshot
sections.body: Inputs are observed twice before compilation so an editor save sequence does not publish a mixture of old and new files.

sections.title: Never replace validity with a partial edit
sections.body: A parser error, invalid token document, or failed group publication leaves the previous complete artifact set in place.

documents.title: Plan first. Authorize exact bytes.
documents.summary: Generate bounded repair proposals, bind authorization to source hashes, verify in staging, then publish receipts.

sections.title: Join findings to a proposal
sections.body: Repair plans name exact finding codes, files, byte ranges, replacements, expected hashes, and verification commands.

sections.title: Verify before mutation
sections.body: Dry-run applies the authorized patch inside a staging copy and executes bounded Rust or browser checks without replacing the source tree.

sections.title: Time and output are part of safety
sections.body: Test, browser, toolchain, and version subprocesses use explicit deadlines and output limits while the repair lock is held.

documents.title: Audit and transform without a framework.
documents.summary: Use PliegoCSS as a standards control layer around an ordinary stylesheet and static HTML build.

sections.title: Start with emitted CSS
sections.body: No adapter is required. Audit the exact stylesheet the browser loads and archive canonical findings beside the build.

sections.title: Transform explicitly
sections.body: Compatibility transformation and minification are separate from analysis so a read-only audit never rewrites authored output.
sections.code:
pliego-cssc transform-css --input src/app.css \
  --output public/app.css --targets modern --format minified

sections.title: Typed authoring is optional
sections.body: Rust applications can compile typed styles into the same static site, but plain HTML consumers only need the final CSS asset.

documents.title: Integrate through files, not hidden hooks.
documents.summary: Vite, webpack, esbuild, CI systems, and custom pipelines consume explicit CSS, manifests, findings, maps, and asset plans.

sections.title: Run PliegoCSS as a producer
sections.body: Invoke compile or transform before the application bundler and pass its ordinary CSS output through the normal asset graph.

sections.title: Consume stable sidecars
sections.body: Use the numbered JSON schemas for manifests, Token Graphs, findings, reachability, project indexes, and Asset Plans instead of scraping terminal text.

sections.title: Keep topology in its owner
sections.body: A framework adapter may export route and component reachability. PliegoCSS validates and projects that sidecar but does not crawl application internals.

documents.title: Configuration is part of identity.
documents.summary: Theme, target, format, manifests, reachability, pruning, and token selections are explicit, validated, and hash-bound.

sections.title: Conventional TOML discovery only
sections.body: Without --config, --tokens, or --seed, the CLI searches for pliego.theme.toml from the workspace and input package roots. Ambiguous candidates fail.

sections.title: Selectors are mutually exclusive
sections.body: --config, --tokens, and --seed cannot be combined. JSON token documents are never discovered implicitly.

sections.title: Bind the complete choice
sections.body: Targets, format, emission settings, manifest version, pruning, theme bytes, resolver selections, and reachability bytes participate in the control configuration hash.

documents.title: Stable codes, precise ranges.
documents.summary: Parser, source scanner, composition, policy, invocation, migration, and formatter failures share a canonical transport.

sections.title: Human diagnostics
sections.body: Terminal output favors the next corrective action while retaining the stable code, severity, file, line, column, and byte range.

sections.title: Canonical JSON
sections.body: JSON mode writes one schema-1 document to stderr on failure and leaves stdout empty. Consumers should branch on codes, not localized prose.

sections.title: SARIF for code scanning
sections.body: Audit findings can be serialized as SARIF while preserving canonical rule identity and source regions for hosted review systems.

documents.title: Release truth bound to one exact candidate.
documents.summary: The current 1.0 promotion state is blocked; no historical report can override these source-bound gates.

sections.title: Candidate identity
sections.body: Target 0.1.0; candidate 0.1.0-rc.2; tag v0.1.0-rc.2; commit 064dcbce96a3a5cc97a940d07566c008bb5e2d3e; Git tree 010a64f5d0bbd142a1d015fda4ccf573cc6e4133; observed 2026-07-22T14:10:00Z; expires 2026-07-29T14:10:00Z.

sections.title: Readiness dimensions
sections.body: Technical: blocked; Operational: blocked; Adoption: blocked; Authorized: blocked; Promotion: blocked.

sections.title: Current blockers
sections.body: exact-candidate-ci (pending): GitHub Actions run 29864046865 passed the exact RC.2 commit across Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS with Rust 1.85 and 1.96 plus the listed release jobs, but its promotion window has expired and requires a fresh candidate replay. exact-candidate-codeql (pending): CodeQL run 29864046876 passed Actions, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Rust analysis on the exact RC.2 commit, but its promotion window has expired and requires a fresh candidate replay. g0-corrections-on-candidate (pending): G0 corrections are not part of the exact RC.2 candidate. They require a newly named candidate plus hosted replay before they can become release evidence. browser-release-matrix (blocked): Every required hosted browser lane is not configured for the exact candidate source; local or historical browser runs have no promotion authority. adapter-coexistence-matrix (blocked): RC.2 predates the G6 adapter authority. It has no clean exact-source 21-project HTML/Vite/PliegoRS matrix, Tailwind v3/v4 source/output audit, DOM/ARIA/style equivalence, exact rollback, or pinned PliegoRS framework replay. registry-replay-refresh (pending): RC.2 was previously replayed from crates.io, but schema 3 requires a fresh, unexpired, artifact-hashed replay for the exact promotion candidate. production-deployment-refresh (pending): The production site has historical deployment evidence, but a current exact-source edge and browser replay with hashed artifacts is missing. signed-binary-distribution (blocked): RC.2 predates the repository-only G5 distribution contract. It has no exact-source native archives, checksums, CycloneDX SBOMs, GitHub/Sigstore attestations, immutable GitHub Release, or verified pnpm package asset; npmjs publication is forbidden. external-adoption-evidence (pending): RC.2 predates the G7 authority. Recruitment is open, but the required external interviews, real incidents, and pilots have not been recorded as consented, redacted, reviewed, hash-bound evidence. final-promotion-authorization (not-authorized): Mario has not explicitly authorized publishing final 0.1.0 for this exact source commit and Git tree.

documents.title: External adoption is a measured gate.
documents.summary: G7 is currently blocked. Owned fixtures and synthetic incidents cannot satisfy it.

sections.title: Qualified evidence
sections.body: Interviews: 0/10. Real incidents: 0/20. Completed pilots: 0/3. Independent projects: 0/3. Independent organizations: 0/3.

sections.title: Applications are open
sections.body: Read the [public cohort notice](https://github.com/celiumsai/pliegocss/issues/7) or apply privately at [hello@pliegocss.dev](mailto:hello@pliegocss.dev?subject=G7%20external%20adoption). Do not post names, email addresses, credentials, private repository URLs, proprietary source, transcripts, or incident material on GitHub. A public application is not consent and is not evidence.

sections.title: Admission boundary
sections.body: Only consented, redacted, reviewed external records bound to private source evidence by SHA-256 count. Projects owned by Celiums Solutions, PliegoCSS, or celiumsai do not count.

sections.title: Certified adapter scope
sections.body: The frozen 0.1.x policy covers complete literal class groups in static HTML, Vite 8.1.5, and pinned PliegoRS rendered output against Tailwind CSS 3.4.19 or 4.3.3. Tailwind stays loaded during coexistence. Dynamic classes, arbitrary config/plugin execution, and Tailwind removal are excluded.
